newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot propane surges on stock data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot propane surges on stock data.

text.p: Spot Midwest U.S. propane prices leaped 15 cents a gallon by late Tuesday, reaching the $1.00 mark, after industry data showing a large stock drawdown in the region during the month of October, traders said.

Traders said prices jumped as a direct result of the monthly API propane report released late Monday, which estimated Midwest stocks by late October had fallen over 3.5 million barrels from late September -- leaving only about 12.5 million left in primary storage.
"There's concern that if there's a normally cold winter, propane could become scarce with such low stocks," one Midwest trader said.
He speculated current early-December inventories may have shrunken another two to four million barrels.
Meanwhile, prices of propane in the Gulf Coast trading hub of Mont Belvieu rose 1.50 cents a gallon to between 70.0 cents and 70.50 cents late Tuesday, bolstered by the Conway rally, players said.
The API report showed Gulf Coast stocks rising over a million barrels, traders said.
Prices of Belvieu normal butane were talked 2.50 cents a gallon higher, and 1.25 cents higher in Conway, players said, while isobutane prices gained one cent in both centers.
